nodes.name: Receive Inbound Webhook
nodes.notes: Entry point: listens for POST calls on /wf09242-order. Use the TEST url while building, switch callers to the PRODUCTION url after publishing. Watch out: While building use the TEST url; switch callers to the PRODUCTION url after you publish.

nodes.name: Map to Canonical Schema
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes orderId, kind, payload. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Acknowledge Fast (HTTP 202)
nodes.notes: Sends the HTTP 202 response back to the caller — keep this fast; heavy work happens after/async. Watch out: Only works when the Webhook node's Response Mode is set to 'Using Respond to Webhook node'.

nodes.name: Route by Event Kind
nodes.notes: Routes each item to one of 3 lanes: order.paid, order.cancelled + fallback. Watch out: Unmatched items go to the fallback output; without one they are silently dropped.

nodes.name: Handle 'order.paid' → Google Sheets
nodes.notes: Upserts a row into 'Order Tracker', matched on orderId — re-running with the same key updates the row instead of duplicating it. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Handle 'order.cancelled' → Shopify
nodes.notes: Writes to Shopify (upserts the matching order/customer record) — the commerce system of record for this pipeline. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Shopify access token. Shopify Admin → Settings → Apps → Develop apps → create app → Admin API access token.

nodes.name: Log Unrecognized Kind
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Order Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Consolidate Handling
nodes.notes: Rejoins 3 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

# Process new orders with Shopify and Google Sheets on autopilot

**Pattern:** Order Fulfillment · **Level:** Foundation · **Trigger:** Webhook

## What it does
Process new orders with Shopify and Google Sheets on autopilot. It fires the moment an external system calls its webhook.

## Why it exists
Manual order ops is slow and error-prone; this workflow makes the process repeatable, monitored and hands-off, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow
Receive Inbound Webhook → Map to Canonical Schema → Acknowledge Fast (HTTP 202) → Route by Event Kind → Handle 'order.paid' → Google Sheets → Consolidate Handling

## Use it for
- Teams that want to order fulfillment without manual effort
- Anyone automating order ops in e-commerce
- Replacing a fragile manual process with a reliable workflow

## You get
- Scales without extra headcount
- Keeps your systems in sync
- Saves hours of manual work each week

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2 / service account; Shopify access token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

The optional HMAC check runs before any business logic touches the payload — bad signatures are rejected at the door rather than after work has already been done with untrusted data. Acking fast (HTTP 202) and doing the real work after the response is what stops the sender's webhook delivery from timing out and re-delivering the same event.

## Practice exercises

New to this pattern? Try these in order:

1. Turn on signature verification and trace what a tampered payload does at the 'Signature Valid?' gate.
2. Add a new event kind to the switch and give it its own handler.
3. Remove the fast-ack step and observe how response time changes under a slow downstream write.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Shopify access token**
Shopify Admin → Settings → Apps → Develop apps → create app → Admin API access token.
_Gotcha:_ Grant read/write scopes for the resources used here (orders, products).

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Webhook returns 404**
Cause: Calling the test URL when the workflow is published, or vice versa.
Fix: Test URL works only while 'Listen for test event' is armed; the production URL needs the workflow published.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 When this fails

This starter workflow keeps things simple: no automatic retry or error branch yet. If a node fails, the execution just stops — open n8n's **Executions** tab to see which node and why. Ready to harden it? Turn on **Retry On Fail** (3 tries, 2s backoff) on the Settings tab of each external node, and add an error-output branch to a Slack/email alert — every Production-tier template in this library shows that exact pattern.

## 🔐 Security

Never trust inbound payloads: the webhook path is unguessable. Add header auth or IP allow-listing for defense in depth. Secrets live in n8n credentials — never in node parameters.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your order ops process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.
